nodes.title: Finite-order Weierstrass products
nodes.statement: If Λ has finite rank p, let E_p(w)=(1−w)exp(Σ_{j=1}^p w^j/j) and δ=1 if 0∈Λ, otherwise 0. The products z^δ∏_{λ∈Λ\{0}}E_p(z/λ) converge normally on compact sets to an entire function ΨΛ, with zero set exactly Λ and simple zeros there; its order is at most p+1. Finite order here means a global bound exp(C(1+‖z‖)^d) for some positive C and integer d, which is equivalent to the usual finiteness of entire order.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

nodes.title: Interpolation with vertical strip decay
nodes.statement: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space, Ψ an entire function on ℂ of finite order, and q:Uℂ→ℂ polynomial. There is an entire ν with exactly the zero set q^{-1}(Ψ^{-1}(0)) and with rapid decay on every vertical strip: for every M>0 and r∈ℕ, sup_{‖Re z‖≤M}(1+‖z‖)^r|ν(z)|<∞. Consequently this holds for q^{-1}(Λ) when Λ has finite rank. If L⊂Uℂ is generated by complex-linearly independent vectors and A⊂Uℂ is finite, there is such a vertically moderate ν vanishing on L\A and nonzero at every point of A; no vanishing requirement is imposed off L. The same conclusion holds for an affine translate of L, by translating the variable and the finite exceptional set. This is not asserted for an arbitrary lattice of the underlying real space of Uℂ.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space, Ψ an entire function on ℂ of finite order, and q:Uℂ→ℂ polynomial.

proofSteps: In coordinates choose an odd q₀ sufficiently large and multiply Ψ(q(z)) by exp(Σ z_j^{2q₀}); its real part is negative in every imaginary direction outside a bounded set in a fixed strip.

For the lattice statement use complex coordinate functionals integral on its complex-linearly independent generators, remove finitely many exceptional zeros, and multiply the resulting factors; a finite polynomial handles points of A outside the lattice. For an affine lattice first translate its base point to zero; translation preserves the strip-growth conditions.
acceptance: The imaginary-axis Gaussian exp(z²) decays rapidly; exp(−z²) does not.
For L=ℤ and A={0}, the factor sin(πz)/(πz) has the desired zeros; damping supplies the required strip decay.

nodes.title: Real-form involutions and shifted lattices
nodes.statement: Import a based root datum (X*,Φ,X_*,Φ∨), its finite Weyl group W and real Cartan dual h*=X*⊗ℝ. For a real form choose its action ϑ₀ on the datum and put θ={wϑ₀:w∈W,(wϑ₀)²=1}; this finite W-conjugation-stable set is the real-form set. For ϑ∈θ let h*ϑ and h*−ϑ be its ±1 eigenspaces and Yϑ=pr_{−ϑ}(ρ+X*), a discrete affine lattice in h*−ϑ. For each maximal real torus the split/compact decomposition gives an involution in θ; θG is the subset realized by such tori. Abstract Cartan identifications are taken modulo W.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

nodes.title: Holomorphic extension and strip estimates
nodes.statement: Every S∈S_pol extends uniquely to a continuous operator on entire functions with their compact-open topology. There are M_S>0 and a real exponent shift r_S≥0 such that, for all M>0,r∈ℝ, p_{1,M,r}(Sμ)≤C p_{1,M+M_S,r+r_S}(μ); the analogous maximum over θ holds for a real-form coset θ. A rational-coefficient difference operator preserving polynomials has poles only along affine reflection hyperplanes and belongs to S. If μ vanishes on H_s, μ/ℓ_s is entire and satisfies the corresponding widened-strip estimate without an extra polynomial exponent.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

proofSteps: Use Taylor polynomials for compact-open density and integral division in a transverse direction for a vanishing numerator. Bound the whole unit disk in that direction, not only a fixed endpoint.
When a reflection commutes with ϑ use the companion involution sϑ in the same real-form coset; the general finite W-stable set alone does not justify this step.
For the localization criterion compare values of polynomials at affine translates at a generic pole and use interpolation to exclude a nonreflection pole.

The estimates use extended seminorms; an arbitrary entire function need not have a finite right-hand side.

nodes.title: Real Schwartz and Sobolev descriptions
nodes.statement: Take the real-group factor of AF.0/adelic-schwartz-space. Its elements are smooth functions for which Df is bounded for every algebraic differential operator D on G(ℝ). The seminorm topology is nuclear Fréchet and equals the topology defined by ‖Df‖₂ for all algebraic D, using distributional derivatives for the converse. The comparison is with Nash Schwartz functions, not merely Harish-Chandra C²(G). There is a continuous inclusion S(G)⊂⋂_{p>0}C^p(G), with equality precisely when the algebraic centre of G is compact at the real points. For an additive real vector group the resulting polynomial derivative conditions agree with Mathlib SchwartzMap.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: Take the real-group factor of AF.0/adelic-schwartz-space.

proofSteps: Compare algebraic differential operators to polynomially weighted invariant derivatives in finitely many algebraic charts.
Use local Sobolev estimates and polynomial volume growth in algebraic height for the L²/bounded comparison; identify the required Nash chart and partition input in G1.
Use the standard comparison with Harish-Chandra seminorms, keeping the noncompact central directions.
acceptance: On a split real torus, decay in the logarithm of the torus coordinate alone does not give Nash Schwartz decay.
For a compact real reductive group this space is C∞ with its usual topology.

For every fixed finite left/right K-type set and compact-support stage, the map is continuous to the corresponding finite-K-type Schwartz space. The output need not be compactly supported. The W-invariance hypothesis is mandatory.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

proofSteps: Use Delorme’s semisimple rapid-symbol theorem as the exact requested AS.6 strengthening R3; compact Paley–Wiener alone is not declared to supply it.

Split-centre Fourier–Laplace theory and the Schwartz tensor theorem identify the rapid-symbol tensor factors (Lemma A.2); extend separately continuous bilinear maps between the fixed Fréchet stages jointly, then use AS.0 tensor universality. Extend to finitely many components by K/K⁰.

nodes.title: Kostant centralizers and translated characters
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional algebraic representation τ of G, Rτ=(U(g)⊗End τ)^{δg} is finite free over Z(g), and after a basis is chosen δ(z)=Σ_i S_i(z)v_i with S_i∈S_pol. If Λ(τ) is the finite weight set and t_λf(α)=f(α−λ), then ∏_{λ∈Λ(τ)}(δ(z)−t_{−λ}z)=0: its roots are α↦z(α+λ). The resulting difference operators have the strip estimates of SM.0. Freeness and this annihilator are Kostant inputs, requested from AF.1 rather than redeveloping enveloping-algebra representation theory here.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §2.4, Lemma 2.22 and its proof, p.16; Kostant 1975, Theorems 4.8–4.9, as cited there

proofSteps: Apply the exact finite-free centralizer and tensor-character annihilator contract R4.

nodes.title: Generic semisimplicity after tensoring
nodes.statement: For a minimal parabolic P=MAN, finite-dimensional algebraic τ, and an irreducible representation ξ of the compact-mod-centre M, the principal-series family I_P(ξ,λ)⊗τ is semisimple for λ outside a locally finite exceptional union of affine analytic hyperplanes. Its constituents have the translated infinitesimal characters prescribed by the weights of τ. The assertion is generic, not at every singular inducing parameter.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

nodes.title: L² estimates for rapid-symbol multipliers
nodes.statement: For μ∈N_{θ∪{1}}^W the compact-support multiplier extends uniquely to a continuous multiplier on S(G). For each algebraic differential operator D there is M_D>0 such that for every r∈ℝ a continuous seminorm ν_{D,r} on S(G) satisfies ‖D(μ⋆f)‖₂≤ν_{D,r}(f) max_{ϑ∈θ∪{1}}p_{ϑ,M_D,r}(μ). The transform identity holds on every irreducible admissible representation, not only the tempered dual.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For μ∈N_{θ∪{1}}^W the compact-support multiplier extends uniquely to a continuous multiplier on S(G).

proofSteps: On compact bi-K-finite functions use Plancherel, the inclusion of tempered characters in the shifted imaginary strips (R2), and centralizer difference-operator bounds to estimate multiplication by algebraic coefficients.
Generic principal-series identities and the subquotient theorem transfer the transform formula to all admissible representations.
Density in the L² derivative topology extends the action, and the convolution and continuity identities pass to the limit.
acceptance: Use only containment of the tempered character set in the lattice union; equality is false for compact groups.

nodes.title: Schwartz multipliers of moderate symbols
nodes.statement: For every μ∈M_{θ∪{1}}(h*ℂ)^W there is a unique continuous complex-linear Tμ:S(G)→S(G) such that π(Tμf)=μ(χπ)π(f) for all irreducible admissible π. It is a centroid multiplier: Tμ(f₁*f₂)=Tμ(f₁)*f₂=f₁*Tμ(f₂). The map μ↦Tμ is multiplicative and linear, preserves every finite left/right K-type subspace, and agrees with the AS.6 compact multiplier on the common domain. Its kernel consists of symbols vanishing at actual infinitesimal characters of irreducible admissible representations; no classification of all continuous multipliers is asserted.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §2.3, Theorem 2.13, p.12; §2.4, completion of proof and Remark 2.26, pp.20–21; Remark 2.16, pp.12–13

nodes.title: Finite K-type detection for sharp symbols

Moreover μ⋆ preserves bi-K-finiteness and defines the corresponding multiplier on the algebraic K-finite Schwartz algebra. hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

nodes.title: Adelic LF and finite-place compatibility
nodes.statement: Import S(G(𝔸_F)) from AF.0: at fixed compact finite support C and compact open J it is the Fréchet space of smooth bi-J-invariant functions with every seminorm sup_g ‖g‖^r|R(X)L(Y)f(g)| finite. Identify that stage with a finite direct sum of S(G∞), one copy per finite J-double coset in C. The countable support/level exhaustion is strict LF, convolution is continuous on the appropriate pairs of stages, and C_c∞ is dense. For a finite place set S, S(G(F_S)) is the completed product over real places tensored with locally constant compactly supported finite-place functions; it embeds by hyperspecial units away from S. Different embeddings obey the Hecke normalization vol(K_v)=1.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

proofSteps: Reduce each finite-support finite-level stage to finitely many real Schwartz copies; import generic strict-LF and nuclear-space arguments from AS.0.

nodes.title: Weights on automorphic quotients
nodes.statement: For a standard parabolic P put [G]_P=M_P(F)N_P(𝔸)\G(𝔸), with the AA quotient measure. A weight is a positive measurable w:[G]_P→ℝ_{>0} such that for every compact U⊂G(𝔸) there is C_U≥1 with C_U^{-1}w(x)≤w(xu)≤C_Uw(x) for all x and u∈U. Write w≍w′ for two-sided global constant comparison. Every weight satisfies w(xg)≤Cw(x)‖g‖^N for some C,N and all x,g. Import the proper quotient height n_P(x)=inf_{p∈M_P(F)N_P(𝔸)}‖px‖≥1 and put σ_P=1+log n_P.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

nodes.title: Franke weights and chamber order
nodes.statement: For each λ∈a*₀ construct a weight d_{P,λ} on [G]_P, determined up to ≍, that is comparable with exp⟨λ,H₀(x)⟩ on every standard P-Siegel domain. It obeys d_{P,tλ}≍d_{P,λ}^t, d_{P,λ+η}≍d_{P,λ}d_{P,η}, and d_{P,λ}≪d_{P,η} if λ≺_Pη in the chamber order. For a proper embedding height, n_P≍max_{λ∈Λ^P_ι}d_{P,λ}. If λ is P-dominant, d_{P,λ}(x)≍sup_{γ∈P(F)}exp⟨λ,H₀(γx)⟩. For Q⊂P and P-dominant λ one has d_{Q,λ}≪d_{P,λ} on their common intermediate quotient.

nodes.title: Parabolic depth functions
nodes.statement: For proper standard P⊊Q define d_P^Q=min_{α∈Σ_P^Q}d_{P,α} and d_Q^P=min_{α∈Σ_P^Q}d_{Q,α}, where Σ_P^Q is the finite nonempty root set in n_P/n_Q. On P(F)N_Q(𝔸)\G(𝔸), d_P^Q≪d_Q^P. nodes.title: Smooth LF representations
nodes.statement: An adelic SLF representation V is a smooth G(𝔸_f)-representation with V=⋃_J V^J; each V^J has an SF Fréchet representation structure for G∞, the inclusions for J′⊂J are closed topological embeddings, and V has their locally convex inductive-limit topology. The group action and stage transitions must be compatible. Use AF.1 for SF representations. A closed invariant subspace with its induced topology is SLF; continuous equivariant maps with closed image induce topological isomorphisms from the quotient by their kernels onto the image. A map need not be injective merely because its image is closed. The Schwartz action extends the compactly supported action and V∞=S(G(𝔸))·V for an F-representation before taking smooth vectors.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: An adelic SLF representation V is a smooth G(𝔸_f)-representation with V=⋃_J V^J; each V^J has an SF Fréchet representation structure for G∞, the inclusions for J′⊂J are closed topological embeddings, and V has their locally convex inductive-limit topology.

proofSteps: Fix a compact open K_f and decompose the smooth finite-place action into its countably many K_f-isotypical summands. Each summand is a closed complemented Fréchet subspace of some V^J, and a fixed J admits only finitely many of these types.

Compact averaging projections preserve a closed invariant subspace, so its induced topology agrees with the locally convex direct sum of its closed isotypical Fréchet pieces, as in Lemma 2.5.4.1. Apply Fréchet open mapping to the quotient-to-image map on these pieces and reassemble the direct sum. Extend the integrated action and use AF.1 factorization; no closed-subspace theorem for arbitrary strict LF spaces is invoked.

Combine the large-positive-s constant-term estimate with weighted Hölder interpolation to reach Re s>0; derivatives and weak holomorphy plus boundedness give locally convex holomorphy.
acceptance: The normalization exponent is s−1/2, not s or s+1/2.

nodes.title: Lapid expansion of Harish-Chandra Schwartz functions
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite product of Res_{K_i/F}GL_{n_i} and χ a regular datum represented by (M_P,π). Write Π=I_P^Gπ. There is N>0 such that for every φ∈C([G]) and λ∈ia_P*, the series φ_{Πλ}=Σ_{v∈𝔅}⟨φ,E(v,λ)⟩ E(v,λ) is defined, basis independent, and converges absolutely in T_N([G]). The map λ↦φ_{Πλ} is Schwartz with values in T_N, using all parameter derivatives, and if φ∈C_χ then φ=∫_{ia_P*}φ_{Πλ}dλ. The exponent N is uniform in λ and φ. The statement for arbitrary reductive groups requires Lapid’s hereditary property (HP); it is not asserted unconditionally here.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §2.9.8, Theorem 2.9.8.1, pp.238–239; Lapid Theorem 4.5, p.22, Proposition 5.1, pp.22–24, Corollary 5.7, pp.25–26
sources.match: Let G be a finite product of Res_{K_i/F}GL_{n_i} and χ a regular datum represented by (M_P,π).

proofSteps: Import the exact polynomial derivative bounds for normalized intertwiners and Eisenstein series under (HP) in R8L; finite products and restriction of scalars preserve the needed GL_n contracts.
Factor φ by a compact smooth convolution and use the relative-character basis estimates with Lapid’s Eisenstein majorization for uniform convergence and parameter derivatives.
Apply the cuspidal wave-packet inversion of Lapid Theorem 4.5; regularity places the whole χ-block in its induced-from-cuspidal image.
acceptance: The theorem concerns regular cuspidal support and the displayed GL_n products; it does not assert the noncuspidal Schwartz Paley–Wiener conjecture.

nodes.title: Schwartz convolution kernels and cuspidal parts
nodes.statement: For f∈S(G(𝔸)) define K_{f,P}, K_{f,P,χ} as the smooth integral kernels of R_P(f) and its χ support component on the AA quotient L² spaces. Define K⁰ on the A_P∞-quotient using its δ_P^{1/2} normalization. They satisfy K⁰_{f,P,χ}(x,y)=∫_{A_P∞}K_{f,P,χ}(x,ay)δ_P(a)^{−1/2}da. This construction extends the compactly supported kernels of AS.6 and fixes its pairing convention by (R_P(f)φ)(x)=∫K_{f,P}(x,y)φ(y)dy. Smooth representatives are used; kernel columns come from regularizing δ_y with the appropriate adjoint. Derivatives in either variable agree with the corresponding left/right derivatives of f.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For f∈S(G(𝔸)) define K_{f,P}, K_{f,P,χ} as the smooth integral kernels of R_P(f) and its χ support component on the AA quotient L² spaces.

proofSteps: Use smooth regularization of point distributions, then apply the continuous support projection.
Apply the quotient disintegration measure to descend along A_P∞; use the weighted estimates for absolute convergence.
acceptance: The A_P factor is δ_P^{−1/2}; kernel and measure normalizations must be tested together.

nodes.title: Uniform bounds for cuspidal kernel parts
nodes.statement: There exists N₀>0 such that for every weight w on [G]_P and continuous seminorm q on T_{w n_P^{N₀}} there is a continuous Schwartz seminorm p satisfying Σ_χq(K_{f,P,χ}(·,y))≤p(f)w(y)^{−1}. In particular Σ_χ|K_{f,P,χ}(x,y)|≤p(f)n_P(x)^{N₀}w(x)/w(y). The same pointwise bound holds for Σ_χ|K⁰_{f,P,χ}(x,y)| when x,y∈[G]_P¹=H_P^{-1}(0). The exponent N₀ is chosen before the weight and seminorm.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: There exists N₀>0 such that for every weight w on [G]_P and continuous seminorm q on T_{w n_P^{N₀}} there is a continuous Schwartz seminorm p satisfying Σ_χq(K_{f,P,χ}(·,y))≤p(f)w(y)^{−1}.

proofSteps: First bound R(f):T₀,w→T_{w n^{N′₀}} uniformly in w at the level of the height loss.
Use absolute support summability after a second fixed loss and apply the uniform boundedness principle to the family of support components.
Apply the resulting bound to δ_y, whose weighted variation norm is w(y)^{-1}; integrate the normalized central direction for K⁰.
acceptance: The K⁰ estimate is stated on H_P=0; simply using the same inequality for arbitrary central translates would alter the weight factors.

nodes.title: Spectral expansion of Schwartz kernels
nodes.statement: There exist a continuous seminorm p on S(G(𝔸)) and N≥0 such that for every X,Y∈U(g∞), f∈S and x,y∈G(𝔸)¹, the sum over χ and standard P, with coefficient |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1}, of ∫_{ia_P^{G,*}}Σ_τ |Σ_{v∈𝔅_{P,χ,τ}} R_x(X)E(x,I_P(λ,f)v,λ) overline(R_y(Y)E(y,v,λ))|dλ is at most p(L(X)R(Y)f)n_G(x)^Nn_G(y)^N. Here 𝒫(M_P) is the finite set of parabolics with Levi M_P and 𝔅 is a K-basis in the discrete inducing space with support χ. For arbitrary x,y∈G(𝔸), K⁰_{f,χ}(x,y) is the sum of the same undifferentiated Eisenstein terms with those coefficients and spectral measures. The absolute value is outside the finite sum within each K-type, before summing types and integrating.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: There exist a continuous seminorm p on S(G(𝔸)) and N≥0 such that for every X,Y∈U(g∞), f∈S and x,y∈G(𝔸)¹, the sum over χ and standard P, with coefficient |𝒫(M_P)|^{−1}, of ∫_{ia_P^{G,*}}Σ_τ |Σ_{v∈𝔅_{P,χ,τ}} R_x(X)E(x,I_P(λ,f)v,λ) overline(R_y(Y)E(y,v,λ))|dλ is at most p(L(X)R(Y)f)n_G(x)^Nn_G(y)^N.

proofSteps: Start with the parent compact-kernel spectral identity, retaining its discrete inducing representation space and parabolic multiplicity factors.
Use Arthur factorization at fixed normal finite level, then positivity on the diagonal and Cauchy–Schwarz to bound the grouped K-type terms by the kernel majorant.
Use the uniform boundedness principle and density to pass to Schwartz f and commute group derivatives with the uniformly controlled expansion.
acceptance: Absolute convergence of the ungrouped individual basis terms is not claimed by this estimate.
The derivative estimate uses x,y∈G(𝔸)¹, whereas the displayed kernel identity holds after central disintegration for general x,y.

nodes.title: Level and T-characters
nodes.statement: Fix a number field F, connected reductive G/F, its maximal F-split central torus Z and unitary automorphic central character ω. Fix a finite set S of finite primes containing all ramified group and level places, K=K_S×∏_{v∉S}K_v, and a set T⊃S that may be infinite. H_G^T is the restricted tensor product of the spherical algebras at v∉T, with unit 1_{K_v} and vol(K_v)=1. A T-character χ is a character of Z(g∞)⊗H_G^T, equivalently an infinitesimal-character W-orbit χ∞ and a family of unramified characters away from T. L²_ω[χ] denotes the closed χ-eigenpart in the fixed-level Hilbert space; its cuspidal subspace is intersected with L²_cusp. The normalizations of Z, A_M∞ and unitary unramified twists are compared with AS.1–AS.4.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: Fix a number field F, connected reductive G/F, its maximal F-split central torus Z and unitary automorphic central character ω.

proofSteps: Use the existing central-character quotient and spherical Hecke algebras; form the algebraic restricted tensor with finite-support Hecke operators.
Use the simultaneous central/Hecke eigencondition and compare the normalized cuspidal-datum quotient through R9.
acceptance: T itself may be infinite; each Hecke operator has finite support.

nodes.title: CAP characters relative to T
nodes.statement: For a fixed inner form G′ of G, a T-character χ is (G′,T)-CAP if there is a proper parabolic P′⊊G′ with Levi M′, and a cuspidal automorphic representation σ of M′(𝔸) such that at almost all v∉T the unramified representation determined by χ_v is a constituent of the normalized induction of σ_v, under the unramified inner-form identification. This is an almost-everywhere finite-place condition, independent of χ∞. Non-CAP is its negation. The inner form is a parameter, not an additional existential quantifier. For the non-CAP isolation theorem specialize G′=G and rule out proper cuspidal data of G itself.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For a fixed inner form G′ of G, a T-character χ is (G′,T)-CAP if there is a proper parabolic P′⊊G′ with Levi M′, and a cuspidal automorphic representation σ of M′(𝔸) such that at almost all v∉T the unramified representation determined by χ_v is a constituent of the normalized induction of σ_v, under the unramified inner-form identification.

proofSteps: Fix the inner form parameter, then form the existential predicate over its parabolics and cuspidal representations.
Show independence of changing finitely many local identifications or ramified places; do not add an archimedean matching hypothesis.
acceptance: Exact occurrence in a proper datum implies CAP, but CAP need not imply exact occurrence at every retained place.

nodes.title: Mixed archimedean and spherical multipliers
nodes.statement: A T-multiplier is an element of (M♯θ)^W⊗_ℂH_G^T, acting on fixed-K test functions by the real multiplier in the archimedean factor and spherical convolution in the retained finite factors. Its action is continuous stagewise, remains bi-K-invariant, and obeys R(μ⋆f)=μ(χ)R(f) on an irreducible χ-isotypic representation. Evaluation μ(χ) is well defined on the tensor product. This algebra need not have a unit because the sharp factor may not have one; the Hecke unit alone is not an allowed T-multiplier.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: A T-multiplier is an element of (M♯θ)^W⊗_ℂH_G^T, acting on fixed-K test functions by the real multiplier in the archimedean factor and spherical convolution in the retained finite factors.

proofSteps: Use commutation of real multipliers and finite spherical convolution to descend the action from pure tensors.
Use each local spectral identity and finite sums to prove the scalar action and evaluation rule.
acceptance: All finite-place support changes remain finite, even for infinite T.

nodes.title: Quasi-cuspidal Schwartz test functions
nodes.statement: For the fixed (G,Z,ω,K), a bi-K Schwartz test function f is quasi-cuspidal if R(f) maps the entire Hilbert space L²_ω([G]/K) into its closed cuspidal subspace. This is a property of the integrated operator on that quotient and central character. It does not require every local constant term of f to vanish, nor does it quantify over all central characters.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For the fixed (G,Z,ω,K), a bi-K Schwartz test function f is quasi-cuspidal if R(f) maps the entire Hilbert space L²_ω([G]/K) into its closed cuspidal subspace.

proofSteps: Use the range inclusion in the existing closed cuspidal Hilbert subspace.
Express equivalently that the orthogonal projection onto the cuspidal complement composed with R(f) is zero.
acceptance: The zero operator is quasi-cuspidal even when it is produced by a test function with nonzero local constant terms.

nodes.title: Typical cuspidal data at an infinitesimal character
nodes.statement: For each standard Levi M import the splitting of its Cartan dual into a central quotient c_M*/a_M* and the derived Cartan quotient b_M*. Let γ_M^+,γ_M^− be the corresponding quotient maps, and let λ_M be the derived Casimir polynomial. A normalized cusp representation σ of M is χ∞-typical if γ_M^+(χσ∞) belongs to the finite image γ_M^+(χ∞) and λ_M(γ_M^−(χσ∞)) belongs to the finite set λ_M(γ_M^−(χ∞)). Images of W-orbits are finite sets; choices of representatives do not change membership. Work modulo unitary unramified twists on a_M. Fix a finite set of archimedean K_M-types and a compact open finite level when asserting finiteness.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For each standard Levi M import the splitting of its Cartan dual into a central quotient c_M*/a_M* and the derived Cartan quotient b_M*.

proofSteps: Compare the central cotangent quotient to AA norm-one central ideles and AS normalized twists, retaining the c_M/a_M directions over a general number field.
Apply the central and derived polynomials to every representative in the finite W-orbit.
acceptance: Both conditions are necessary; the derived Casimir alone cannot control a torus.

Separates all non-typical inducing families.

nodes.title: Finite-rank cuspidal Casimir values
nodes.statement: At fixed finite level and a finite set of archimedean K_M-types, the set Λ_M of derived Casimir values of cuspidal representations of M modulo a_M twists is countable and has finite rank as a subset of ℂ. More precisely the needed derived semisimple cuspidal counting function, counted with multiplicity below positive elliptic spectral parameter R, is bounded by C(1+R)^d. To pass from M to M_der, one must use a finite union of conjugate finite levels; the original level intersection alone is not sufficient. Normalize the Casimir sign so that its K-type-adjusted elliptic eigenvalue is nonnegative.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §3.3, Lemma 3.12 and proof, p.26; Donnelly 1982, Theorem 9.1 as invoked there
sources.match: At fixed finite level and a finite set of archimedean K_M-types, the set Λ_M of derived Casimir values of cuspidal representations of M modulo a_M twists is countable and has finite rank as a subset of ℂ.

proofSteps: Request the exact Donnelly polynomial upper bound R7 from AF.3; finite multiplicity alone is not a counting theorem.
Choose finite representatives of M(𝔸)/(M(F)Z_M(𝔸)M_der(𝔸)K_MM∞). Translate a nonzero fixed-level cusp vector by a suitable representative before restricting to M_der.
Intersect the finitely many conjugate derived levels, apply the counting theorem at that common smaller level, and deduce convergence of a sufficiently high reciprocal power sum.
acceptance: A repeated eigenvalue contributes multiplicity to the counting estimate, but only once to the interpolation zero set.

nodes.title: Finiteness of typical cuspidal data
nodes.statement: For each Levi M, fixed ω, fixed finite level and finite K_M-type set, only finitely many χ∞-typical cuspidal representations occur modulo the normalized a_M twists. After fixing ω and normalizing the a_M twists, the allowed central differentials lie in a discrete affine lattice coset in the remaining central directions of c_M,ℂ*/a_M,ℂ*, possibly of rank zero; the first typicality condition restricts them to finitely many values; the remaining finite-component central characters are finite at the fixed level. Donnelly’s bound restricts derived parameters, and fixed infinitesimal/central-character admissibility gives the final finite representation set.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §3.3, Lemma 3.13, p.26, with the central-character step in the proof of Lemma 3.14, pp.26–27
sources.match: For each Levi M, fixed ω, fixed finite level and finite K_M-type set, only finitely many χ∞-typical cuspidal representations occur modulo the normalized a_M twists.

proofSteps: Use the character lattice of the fixed-level compact norm-one central quotient. Compare extension of the fixed ω and normalization of twists as requested in R9: the resulting allowed differentials form an affine coset with complex-linearly independent lattice generators, rather than a full-rank lattice in all of c_M*/a_M*.
Apply both typicality conditions, then derived counting at the conjugate levels and Harish-Chandra fixed-character finiteness.
acceptance: For a torus with trivial derived group the proof must still use the central condition.

nodes.title: Archimedean annihilators of unwanted families
nodes.statement: For each standard Levi M there is μ∞^M∈(M♯θ)^W with μ∞^M(χ∞)≠0 that vanishes on every induced character χ^G_{σ_s∞} for every complex s∈a_M,ℂ* whenever σ has the fixed permitted types and level and is not χ∞-typical. Construct it using finite-rank interpolation in the derived Casimir and interpolation on the allowed affine central lattice coset in c_M,ℂ*/a_M,ℂ*. Multiply by a sharp symbol μ∞⁰ nonzero at every target Weyl translate; the additional moderate factors alone need not be sharp.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For each standard Levi M there is μ∞^M∈(M♯θ)^W with μ∞^M(χ∞)≠0 that vanishes on every induced character χ^G_{σ_s∞} for every complex s∈a_M,ℂ* whenever σ has the fixed permitted types and level and is not χ∞-typical.

proofSteps: Remove from Λ_M the finite target Casimir set, interpolate a function with exactly those unwanted zeros, and pull back along λ_Mγ_M^−.

For the central quotient translate the allowed affine lattice coset to a lattice with complex-linearly independent generators and apply SM.0/vertical-interpolation, killing its points outside the finite target image. Take their product over W and multiply μ∞⁰; the quotient maps kill the full complex a_M inducing direction.

nodes.title: Finite surviving cuspidal components
nodes.statement: For the fixed (G,Z,ω,K,χ∞) there exists μ∞∈(M♯θ)^W with μ∞(χ∞)≠0 such that, for every fixed-K Schwartz f, R(μ∞⋆f) has image in a finite orthogonal sum of AS.1 cuspidal-data components. The list is independent of f. Choose the finite detecting K∞-types supplied by μ∞⁰, propagate them to the finitely many Levi K_M-types and finite levels, retain only typical data, and annihilate all remaining data by the product of μ∞^M.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For the fixed (G,Z,ω,K,χ∞) there exists μ∞∈(M♯θ)^W with μ∞(χ∞)≠0 such that, for every fixed-K Schwartz f, R(μ∞⋆f) has image in a finite orthogonal sum of AS.1 cuspidal-data components.

proofSteps: Use compact-picture Frobenius reciprocity to get finite Levi type sets from the detecting G-types, and choose compatible finite levels including the unramified factors.
Apply the annihilator to every complex induced family and use density of pseudo-Eisenstein series in its cuspidal block.
Finite typicality leaves a finite block list after multiplying the finitely many standard-Levi factors.

nodes.title: Occurrence in a cuspidal datum
nodes.statement: A T-character χ occurs in a normalized cuspidal datum (M,σ) if there is one complex parameter s∈a_M,ℂ* for which the induced infinitesimal character equals χ∞ and, for every finite v outside T, the spherical constituent of the normalized induction I_P^G(σ_s,v) has character χ_v. The same parameter must work at all these places. This property descends to the AS.1 Weyl-and-twist equivalence class. Denote the resulting set by D(G,ω)_χ. Occurrence is stronger than the almost-everywhere finite-place condition in CAP.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

proofSteps: Use normalized induction, its infinitesimal character and the Satake character at each unramified place.
A Weyl conjugacy or normalized unramified twist changes s and the representative without changing existence.

nodes.title: Mixed archimedean and Hecke annihilators
nodes.statement: If χ does not occur in (M,σ), construct a T-multiplier μ_{M,σ} nonzero at χ whose operator annihilates the whole AS.1 cuspidal component L²_(M,σ). Only finitely many places outside T are used, even if T is infinite. For proper M choose representatives α_σ,α_χ and a splitting ℓ:h*→a_M*. For each w∈W the only candidate parameter compatible with α_σ+s=wα_χ is s_w=ℓ(wα_χ)−ℓ(α_σ). Nonoccurrence supplies an invariant archimedean polynomial or a spherical Hecke element at a retained finite place distinguishing the target from that candidate. Its values along the induced family are exponential polynomials in s. A finite linear combination avoiding the finitely many target-zero hyperplanes, followed by a Weyl product, vanishes on the entire family and is nonzero at χ. Multiply by a moderate damping and a sharp seed to obtain an element of (M♯θ)^W⊗H_G^T.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: If χ does not occur in (M,σ), construct a T-multiplier μ_{M,σ} nonzero at χ whose operator annihilates the whole AS.1 cuspidal component L²_(M,σ).

proofSteps: If the fixed-level component is zero there is nothing to annihilate; use a sharp seed nonzero at χ.

For M=G an archimedean invariant polynomial separates unequal infinitesimal characters; otherwise choose a Hecke element separating the finite-place characters and multiply it by a sharp seed. A bare Hecke element need not lie in the sharp tensor algebra.

For proper M form the finite exponential-polynomial differences by subtracting their evaluations at s=ℓ(w′α)−ℓ(α_σ). Choose one linear combination nonzero at every target Weyl translate, then multiply over w′. Along α=α_σ+s its identity factor vanishes.

Choose a W-invariant entire damping nonzero at χ∞ that changes the exponential coefficients to moderate strip growth, and multiply by the sharp seed. Use the scalar action on induced representations and density of pseudo-Eisenstein series to annihilate the closed component.
acceptance: Annihilation holds for every complex s, not just unitary parameters.
The multiplier remains in the nonunital sharp algebra.

nodes.title: Isolation of occurring cuspidal components
nodes.statement: For every T-character χ and the fixed (G,Z,ω,S,K), there is a T-multiplier μ with μ(χ)=1 such that for every f∈S(G(𝔸))^K the image of R(μ⋆f) on L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)/K,ω) lies in the Hilbert orthogonal sum of the AS.1 cuspidal components indexed by D(G,ω)_χ. The constructed range is already contained in a finite sum of these components. The identity μ(χ)=1 preserves the action of f on any admissible representation with this T-character, including one absent from the automorphic spectrum. This theorem asserts a range constraint and scalar normalization; it does not assert that μ acts as the identity on each entire surviving component.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.match: For every T-character χ and the fixed (G,Z,ω,S,K), there is a T-multiplier μ with μ(χ)=1 such that for every f∈S(G(𝔸))^K the image of R(μ⋆f) on L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)/K,ω) lies in the Hilbert orthogonal sum of the AS.1 cuspidal components indexed by D(G,ω)_χ.

proofSteps: Start with μ∞ from SM.4 and its finite list of surviving equivalence classes.
Multiply by the mixed annihilator for each class where χ does not occur. All factors are nonzero at χ.
Divide by the resulting scalar at χ; use the AS.4 orthogonal decomposition and commuting scalar actions to prove the range inclusion.
acceptance: Check that no finite-place factor outside a finite set is introduced.
No orthogonal-projection or idempotence conclusion is inferred.

nodes.title: Isolation of non-CAP cuspidal spectrum
nodes.statement: If χ is not (G,T)-CAP, choose the normalized multiplier of global isolation so that for every fixed-K Schwartz f its operator on the entire central-character L² space has image in L²_cusp[χ]. In particular μ⋆f is ω-quasi-cuspidal and μ(χ)=1. Without the non-CAP hypothesis the same normalized multiplier has this range property after restricting its domain to L²_cusp. Here L²_cusp[χ] is the maximal closed cuspidal subspace on whose smooth vectors Z(g)⊗H_G^T acts by χ; neither assertion requires χ to be automorphic.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §3.1, Theorems 3.6–3.7, p.23; their proofs in §3.4, p.30
sources.match: If χ is not (G,T)-CAP, choose the normalized multiplier of global isolation so that for every fixed-K Schwartz f its operator on the entire central-character L² space has image in L²_cusp[χ].

proofSteps: A proper cuspidal datum with occurrence would imply CAP, so only M=G can survive in the non-CAP case.
Intersect the occurring component sum with L²_cusp. Orthogonality of the AS.1 decomposition identifies that intersection with L²_cusp[χ].
For arbitrary χ restrict the operator to the invariant cuspidal subspace before taking the intersection.
acceptance: In the unrestricted-character assertion only the cuspidal domain is controlled.
Quasi-cuspidality is asserted on the whole L² space only in the non-CAP case.

nodes.title: Preservation of a non-CAP admissible representation
nodes.statement: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of G(𝔸) with unitary automorphic central character. Suppose π is not nearly equivalent to a constituent of induction from any proper cuspidal datum. At a finite level K choose finite S containing every ramified place of G, K and π and take T=S. The normalized isolation multiplier satisfies π(μ⋆f)=π(f) for every fixed-K Schwartz f, and its global L² operator has image in the π-nearly isotypic cuspidal subspace. The sharper χπ^T-eigenspace range may be used as an intermediate inclusion. If the nearly isotypic cuspidal subspace is zero, the global L² action is zero while the action on π is still preserved.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

sources.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2(4), p.2; §3.1, Theorem 3.6, p.23
sources.match: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of G(𝔸) with unitary automorphic central character.

proofSteps: Associate the unramified Hecke and infinitesimal T-character to π.
Non-CAP for π gives the hypothesis of SM.5 non-CAP isolation. Equality of all Hecke characters outside finite S implies local isomorphism there by the spherical classification.
The multiplier evaluates to 1 at χπ, so the scalar action preserves π(f).
acceptance: Near equivalence does not determine the infinitesimal character for a general reductive group.
No automorphic occurrence of π is assumed.

nodes.title: Isolation of one GLₙ cuspidal-support component
nodes.statement: For G=Res_{F′/F}GL_n and an irreducible admissible π occurring as a constituent of normalized induction of a cuspidal representation σ of a Levi M, with unitary automorphic central character, there is a normalized multiplier preserving π(f) and mapping the entire central-character L² space into the single AS.1 cuspidal-support component attached to (M,σ), for every fixed-K Schwartz f. The correct uniqueness input is the isobaric strong multiplicity-one theorem: the almost-everywhere unramified characters determine the multiset of cuspidal constituents, with their unramified norm twists. It identifies the cuspidal datum, not every irreducible constituent of its induced representation.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.

proofSteps: Use isobaric strong multiplicity one from AL.3, including normalization and twists, to show that the occurrence set contains only the inducing cuspidal-support equivalence class.
Apply global isolation with χ=χπ^S and normalize at π.
acceptance: Do not replace isobaric strong multiplicity one by the cuspidal-only Piatetski-Shapiro 1979 theorem.
The target is a coarse cuspidal-support component and may include continuous and residual spectrum.

nodes.title: Isolation of refined discrete-data components
nodes.statement: Replace AS.1 cuspidal data by AS.4 Langlands data (M,σ) with σ in the discrete automorphic spectrum of M, using its normalized unramified-twist and Weyl equivalence. Assuming the polynomial fixed-level, fixed-K-type discrete-spectrum Casimir counting input R8D, there is a T-multiplier with value 1 at χ whose L² range lies in the sum of the refined Langlands components where χ occurs, defined by the same simultaneous character equations. This can be strictly smaller than the coarse cuspidal-support range. The extra polynomial counting theorem is a required input, not a consequence of mere discreteness or of a general trace-class ideal theorem.
hypotheses: The conventions in the roadmap introduction apply; all additional hypotheses are in the statement.
